result:
`build_invoice` now looks up each country's tax rate once per call instead of once per line. I haven't timed it on Northwind's real October data. The speedup is expected but unmeasured.

Each lookup re-read both tax JSON files from disk, once for every line. The change is in `meterbill/invoices/builder.py`. Within one call the tenant and issue date are fixed, so the rate depends only on the country. A dict local to the call holds those rates and is dropped when the call returns.

Nothing is cached across calls. Decision #7 forbids that: a long-running worker kept using a revoked exemption from `tax_overrides.json` for six hours. It also rules out invalidating by file mtime, because rsync preserves mtimes. Each `build_invoice` call still reads the current files, so rates and errors come out the same as before.

I added a test in `tests/test_invoices.py`. It checks that one call does one lookup per country and that a second call looks up again. The full suite passes (377 tests).

I closed #8 in clarity with a note on the approach, since it was the idea for exactly this change.

If the run is still slow, the cost may have moved to the repeated reads inside a single call. In that case, profile a real October run before changing anything else.
